serveur.apprendre.consigne:
Learn mode is on: the user is not a developer and wants to understand by watching you work.
At every step that matters, explain in one or two simple sentences what you are doing and why, without jargon (define any unavoidable technical term in a few words). Write each explanation as a Markdown callout, separate from the rest of your text:
> [!apprendre] What I am doing
> One or two sentences: what I am doing, then why.
No callout for a trivial action; at most one per step. The work, the precautions and the rest of these instructions do not change.
In your <fiche> block, after prochain_pas, add the line `retenir:` with exactly three short points separated by “;”: what the user can take away from this session for their next piece of work.

serveur.reflexes.bloc_avertissement: Below, `orch` stands for the command `{orch}`. Block offered by GoldenBrain and added with the user's consent; do not edit it by hand. Status, update or removal: `orch reflexes`. Full guide: `orch guide`.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_conclure: **Conclude every turn**: done (`terminee`), or ONE precise human request in `prochain_pas` (closed question or choice, `en_attente`), or a named wait (sub-task, other task, queue). Never a "reste: …" sheet with nobody asked: GoldenBrain would send "conclude" back to you (twice at most) then hand the task back to the user. A delivery awaiting integration is not a human wait: link it (`alimente`) to the integration task. **Waiting for a process**: never with `pgrep -f` on a pattern that appears in your own instructions (it sees itself and never ends); run the command in the foreground, or wait on its PID (`wait`, `tail --pid`). Give the station back (`orch poste liberer`) as soon as the test is over; with no live gate, a reservation lapses after 20 min.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_decision: **The user decides**: no change of status, place or structure without their consent; you propose, they approve.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_etape: **Checkpoint every step**: on your working branch, commit a checkpoint at every milestone and before any long check (full gate, interface); an interrupted session must be able to resume without losing anything.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_etiquettes: **Labels**: read those of your task and of linked tasks, follow a label's instruction, and prefer an existing label to a new one. You do not create labels: you propose them (`orch proposer etiquette <id> <word> --motif "<why>"`) and the user accepts. A shared label steers links between tasks.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_lier: **Link what belongs together**: a task that feeds another, waits for another or relates to it gets linked (`orch proposer lier <id> alimente|prerequis|voir_aussi <cible> --motif "<why>"`); notes and documents are cited in the summary. Routine steps — link, attach, move, rename, due date, task created under yours (`ticket`) — are applied automatically, noted in “Traces” and can be undone by the user from Decisions: propose them without waiting, with an exact reason. The user still decides the steps that commit: closing or changing a status, making a project or an operation, changing a scope, a change of course, any outgoing step. A task that delivers code or a branch feeds the project's integration task: GoldenBrain sets this link at creation when the project declares it (`integration:` in its `contexte.md`); otherwise, `orch proposer lier <id> alimente <integration>`.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_ranger: **Tidy rather than pile up**: short work (no deliverable or branch of its own, same goal as its task) is a LINE of that task — `orch ligne <id> "<what was done>"` — not a task; likewise an audit follow-up or something left to do on your task: a line, not a task proposal (a `tache` proposal from you becomes a line of your task anyway). At most 10 open tasks directly under one parent (adjustable); if a creation is refused for that reason, tidy up (line of an existing task, subgroup, grouping) before insisting. Three kinds, never mixed under one parent: development (code, branch, integration), operations (mail, account, routine, procedure), steering (strategy, communication, name, licence, decision). To file existing tasks under a parent (or detach them), propose `orch proposer rattacher <id> <parent|racine> [--aussi <id>…] --motif "<why>"`: one step for the whole batch; refused on a cycle, a running task, another project, the cap or mixed kinds.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_resultat: **Write down the result when work ends**: what is done, where the deliverable is, what remains — `orch tracer <id> "Result: …"`.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_tache: **Every work request is attached to a GoldenBrain task.** First look for a matching open task (`orch rapprochement "<title>"`, `orch chercher "<words>"`) and resume it; otherwise create one (`orch creer "<title>" --description "<one sentence>"`). A mere conversation is not a task.
serveur.reflexes.bloc_tracer: **Every document created or modified is recorded in the task's sheet**: `orch tracer <id> "<what was done>" --document <path>` (repeatable). A vault document becomes a link there. **Declare your deliverables** (file, page, branch, commit): `orch livrable <id> <path|url>`.

telegram_aide.nom_bloque: Wrong name? Go back to the access key step and enter the right bot’s key. Error 409: another program is already reading this bot, stop it first (a bot allows only one reader).
telegram_aide.nom_pourquoi: Confirming avoids connecting the wrong bot (for example a test bot instead of the capture bot).
telegram_aide.nom_quoi: GoldenBrain asks Telegram and shows the name of the bot this access key controls.
telegram_aide.test_bloque: Nothing received? Open the chat with the bot in Telegram (press “Start” if needed) and try again.
telegram_aide.test_pourquoi: It is the only end-to-end proof: valid access key, right chat, sending works.
telegram_aide.test_quoi: GoldenBrain sends a welcome message to your chat. If you receive it in Telegram, everything is connected; finishing then switches the connection on.
telegram_aide.webhook_bloque: If the old program puts the automatic link back, stop it at the source. Nothing else to do here.
telegram_aide.webhook_pourquoi: A bot can only be read in one way. Turning off the automatic link deletes no waiting message; the old program will simply stop receiving them.
telegram_aide.webhook_quoi: This bot is still linked to an old program (an automatic link, for example an n8n automation). As long as it is, Telegram refuses to deliver messages to GoldenBrain.
